findings.reason: the section either drops the log sentence or states the arm-log header as its own deliverable; leaving it makes the node's gate unmeetable by its stated change and spreads the de-dup node into unrelated logging work.
findings.text: s50's done-when appends "Each arm's log sits under the run directory and carries its revision, its literal command and a closing `EXIT=` line", a requirement the de-duplication deliverable does not produce: `_arm` opens an in-place arm log and writes only the captured output plus `EXIT=<code>` (landing_measure.py:767-771, 813-817), while the `# revision:` / `# command:` header exists only on the partitioned submission script (landing_measure.py:1022-1023), so a worker reading the done-when literally must also change `_arm`'s in-place logging to make its own gate pass — a second deliverable under one verdict — and a worker who reads it as evidence placement will fail a case changes nothing about.

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `reckon/crew/landing_measure.py` and the new test path `tests/test_a_landing_population_names_each_file_once.py` resolve as a source file and an intentionally-absent new test; `tests/test_magnetisation.py` names another project's landing, so it is incident evidence rather than a path this node opens, and the mechanism reproduces here independently.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — s50's negative control can fail (the duplicate is reproducible at base, quoted below), but the done-when's second sentence asks each arm's log to carry its revision and literal command, which no arm written by the named deliverable does in place — see the single_goal finding.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the done-when places each arm's log under the run directory the measurement writes, not a session scratchpad; the gate's own log is the dispatcher's.
rubric_items.naming: pass — `test_a_landing_population_names_each_file_once.py` and the section's prose are mechanism-named, carrying no plan label, stage name or ticket number.
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — the stated root cause matches the code: `population_command = [*argv, *files, "-n", ...] (landing_measure.py:1210) appends the importer population to an armed argv that already names the node's test files, and `importer_population` (landing_measure.py:518-533) includes a test file that imports a changed module even when it is the node's own armed test, so one file is named twice; the endpoint is checkable and the negative control reproduces.
rubric_items.single_goal: a finding — s50's done-when bundles the de-duplication deliverable with a second requirement on arm-log content that is neither part of it nor true of in-place arms.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — s50 is declared `implementable`, is listed in `plan-section-depends-on` for s10 (plan.html:24) beside s46–s49, and the open followup `f-dwl-s50` (plan.html:407) names all five sections, so the chain a coordinator follows reaches s50.
